meta.title: Email Marketing Demystified: Build a Massive Mailing List, Write Copy that Converts and Generate More Sales
meta.author: Matthew Paulson

sentences: **Email Marketing Demystified** is a book that provides a comprehensive guide to email marketing, outlining its effectiveness in modern-day business.
Despite changes in technology and the rise of social media, email remains a powerful communication tool.
With over 7 billion email accounts expected by 2021, the potential reach and engagement email offers are significant.
This book details strategies for building mailing lists, creating engaging content, and monetizing effectively.
It stresses that when done right, **email marketing** can significantly boost **sales** and your connection with your **audience**.
**Email Marketing** has a **massive ROI**; businesses earn $43 for every $1 invested.
It's the most effective for **lead acquisition** and **customer retention**.
Email marketing provides **long-term results**.
Building a subscriber list is a **lasting asset** for revenue generation.
**Most Customers** prefer **email** as a communication channel.
**72%** favor email from companies, and 95% find it useful.
Email marketing outperforms **social media**; it's 40 times better for customer acquisition.
**Marketers** believe in its excellent ROI more than in social media.

parts.title: Building and Optimizing Email Sign-Up Forms

sentences: **MarketBeat** sends **40 million emails** monthly and generates over **5 million page views** with total revenue jumping from **$6 million in 2018** to **$8 million in 2019**.
Growing your email list through website sign-ups is emphasized, highlighting the use of **lead magnets** to entice visitors despite fears of spam.
Examples include **free reports** or discounts.
For effective conversion, create opt-in forms with compelling **headlines** and **descriptions** that set expectations for your emails.
**Button text matters**—even simple changes like using "Show Me Outfits I’ll Love" over "Sign Up Now" can significantly increase clicks.
Consider testing **different placements** like pop-ups (entry or exit), welcome pages, and sidebars to see what maximizes subscriber sign-ups without affecting user experience.
**Thank you pages** are valuable for capturing new actions from users.
Users who reach these pages are already **interested** and more likely to **click ads** or signup for services.
Opt-in forms are crucial for building a **profitable email list**.
They minimize upfront costs compared to other methods, as subscribers through your site are essentially **free**.
Create compelling copy and a desirable **lead magnet** to boost your mailing list growth.
**Testing** opt-in forms' efficiency through split-tests is advised to improve rates.
**Bidsketch** uses email marketing to convert website visitors into **customers**.
Instead of pushing for trials, they focus on getting **email sign-ups** using various **lead magnets** like sample proposals.
Their **Drip campaign** drives conversions by educating users on using proposals efficiently.
Surveys and **JTBD interviews** are utilized to understand customer needs and tailor content effectively.
Bidsketch credits their **mailing list** for a significant portion of their customers and advocates for experimenting with email processes to enhance marketing.
**Growing your list outside your website** involves strategies requiring **investment**.
Co-registration ads allow partnering on **thank you pages** on other sites.
They may cost more but improve **subscriber quality**.
Co-registration and **lead generation** must be monitored for effectiveness.
Bids for subscribers should target those that bring better **returns**.
Swap emails with similar site owners and utilize online tools like **Safe Swaps** to manage this.
**Email rentals** involve renting ad space on another’s email blasts.
Compromise quality by renting rather than buying email addresses.
**Creative ways** to expand your list include **social media** and **event strategies**.
Run **contests** or use **QR codes** on physical marketing.
Utilize **online platforms** like YouTube for call-to-actions.
Implementing **Google AdWords** or leveraging **trade shows** can also serve as effective list-building methods.
Routinely revisit and refresh your list-building tactics to maintain **engagement** and **subscriber growth**.
**Fossett** highlights the importance of **testing** various aspects of your **email marketing** campaign such as **subject lines**, **from-addresses**, and **calls-to-action**.
He emphasizes that different **sending frequencies of your autoresponder series** can greatly impact **engagement** and **sales**.
Testing these components helps identify what resonates most with your audience.
Also, using **email** effectively is crucial for business success.
Fossett shares GMB Fitness' remarkable growth, managing a list of **60,000 subscribers** with **a 60%** open rate, achieving **80% of sales** through email subscribers.
He advises that **email marketing** generates **high ROI** because it reaches **almost everyone online** and is **cost-effective**.
**Your footer** is crucial for staying compliant with anti-spam laws; it includes things like your **unsubscribe link** and **company details**.
Every email should have a **purpose**—whether it's an **announcement**, engaging with users, promoting products, or gathering **feedback**.
When emailing, you should follow the principle of "**Give, Give, Give, Ask**", meaning provide value before asking for something.
This approach makes subscribers more open to purchase your products.
**Effective subject lines** are key to getting your emails opened.
Techniques like **emphasizing important words**, making **personalized**, or displaying **numbers** can greatly enhance open rates.
Always test different strategies to see what works best for your audience.
Whether promoting content, seeking feedback, or sharing announcements, the tone and content should align with the audience's interests and provide clear, concise information.
To keep **email deliverability** high, use techniques like **SPF**, **DKIM**, and **DMARC** records to verify your domain's legitimacy.
**Double opt-in** can reduce invalid sign-ups, but some marketers shift to **single opt-in** for faster list growth despite the engagement trade-off.
**User engagement** (opens, clicks, replies) profoundly impacts whether emails land in inboxes or spam.
Regularly clean your list, removing unengaged subscribers, as ISPs prioritize emails from domains with higher engagement.
Monitor **blacklists** through **MultiRBL** to ensure optimal delivery and resolve spam complaints, maintaining a rate below 0.1%.

parts.title: Optimal Timing and Deliverability in Email Marketing

sentences: When **sending emails** to a **mailing list**, consider the best **times** to send your **messages** for better engagement – **Tuesday**, **Wednesday**, and **Thursday mornings** around **8:00 AM** or in the **evening** around **4:00 PM** can be more effective.
Use tools like **Mail Tester** to **check** your message's **content** for any **spam triggers** before sending.
To avoid having your emails end up in Gmail’s **Promotions** tab, request that subscribers move your email to their **Primary** tab and encourage them to **reply** to your messages.
When starting email prospecting, aim to send **5-10 cold emails each week** through a personal account due to the low volume.
**Personalization** is key; avoid form letters.
If you get a positive response, arrange a **call or meeting** to discuss business.
If no interest is shown, move on.
If there's **no response** after 4-5 days, send a **follow-up email**.
If there's still no reply after a third attempt and they're a good lead, move on.
Prioritize **multiple prospects** over focusing on a single one, given the vast pool of potential customers.
